findings.title: Selecting the first parseable review can discard blocking findings
findings.problem: parseReviewText accepts a schema-valid object found anywhere in the response without checking for competing reviews. In particular, fenced objects are tried before an unfenced final verdict. A quoted example with empty findings can therefore override the actual review containing blockers, and runReview posts success.
findings.failure_scenario: The model returns a fenced example containing {"assessment":"Example","findings":[]}, followed by its actual unfenced review containing a valid blocker finding. Parsing the whole response fails, the example is accepted, and the blocker is discarded. None of the added tests exercises conflicting review objects.
findings.fix: Allow only an unambiguous review result. Preserve support for a single optional fence or preamble, but reject responses containing multiple schema-valid review objects rather than selecting one. Add end-to-end negative tests with a fenced empty example followed by a blocking final review.

findings.title: Marketing-page source changes are missing from the selector
findings.problem: PAGE_SOURCES omits actual public-page inputs, including src/landing.jsx and the learn-content modules such as ops/learn-clinical.mjs and ops/learn-exam.mjs. Changes to these files can alter published marketing pages while marketingPagesChanged returns false. Even under the proposed narrowed policy, these changes require review.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR changes only homepage copy in pulsern/src/landing.jsx or article content in pulsern/ops/learn-clinical.mjs. The build produces changed public content, but the selector compares committed filenames, not generated working-tree changes. Both seo:adversary and report enforcement are skipped.
findings.fix: Cover the actual public-page dependency graph, including homepage sources and all imported article-content modules. Add regression tests for changes confined to these inputs, without requiring generated HTML to be committed in the same change.

findings.title: Git-quoted filenames silently bypass page-change detection
findings.problem: git diff --name-only emits quoted, escaped filenames for non-ASCII characters and control characters. The new script treats those display strings as literal paths, so they no longer start with pulsern/public/ and are classified as unrelated changes. The push comparison has the same defect.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR changes only pulsern/public/révision.html. With Git's default quoting, the emitted filename is surrounded by quotes and contains escaped UTF-8 bytes. The selector returns changed=false, allowing the search gate to finish without the required page review or report.
findings.fix: Read filenames using git diff --name-only -z and parse NUL-delimited paths verbatim. Pipe or store that output without passing NUL bytes through a Bash variable. Add a test using real Git output for an accented public-page filename and a filename containing a tab or newline.

assessment: Do not merge yet. The new response parser can discard blocking findings and publish a PASS. The search-review selector also silently misses legitimate marketing-page changes through both incomplete source coverage and Git filename quoting.
